title: CLO 2025.0 - Modes & Editor
description: This video will introduce the updates related to the editor and modes, which further simplify the workflow and allow you to create freely according to your needs.
transcript:
This video introduces the mode and editor update for you.  
In version 2025.0, we optimized some functions of the chess editor.  
Next, let's take a look at its updates through a file.  

Now you can use a shortcut key to quickly open the chess editor window.  
Just press the letter O on the keyboard to open the chess editor.  
This is the same as in the previous version.  

When you hover the mouse over the object window,  
on the color block of any material,  
you will see that it is just a prompt text using the color of the chess.  

Version 2025.0 is based on this.  
It adds the function of directly switching the color of a single color block.  
You don’t need to open the chess editor to quickly switch the color.  

In addition to fabric, you can also select the color blocks under other materials,  
for example, buttons or names used on the costume.  
By clicking on the color block, you can directly switch to the desired color.  

Now in the chess editor,  
you can directly see the front and side of the fabric.  
And based on the need to change or apply color and texture to a specific surface,  

first, if you look at the color block of color block 2,  
you can see it is divided into three parts.  
If you select the back or side of the fabric in the option card,  
it will select the same material as the front.  
Then you can use the corresponding color blocks in the single-color chess editor  
to edit the color and texture of the front, back, and side.  

As shown in the chess editor,  
the texture is divided by surface.  
From top to bottom are the front, side, and back of the fabric.  

In addition, if the back or side materials are different from the front,  
only the different surfaces will be displayed as separate color blocks.  

As shown in chess editor 3,  
only the reverse settings are different from the front.  
Therefore, it is displayed as two color blocks,  
one representing the front and one representing the reverse.  

If you want a certain fabric where all surface colors and textures are the same as the front,  
you only need to select the corresponding fabric in the object window and click on it.  
By using the same material options as the front,  
you will immediately see in the chess editor  
the color block in the window and a color block.  

From this version,  
when you apply color and texture to an independent component,  
for example, when you apply color and texture to an independent component,  
these components will be displayed in the chess editor in a tree-shaped structure,  
which is convenient for viewing and editing.  

For example, this is a pig’s nose button.  
This pig’s nose button is created as a separate component.  
Next to its name, a small arrow will be displayed.  
When you click on it,  
it will display the color blocks of each component separately.  
When you click on a color block,  
the corresponding part will be displayed in the 3D window.  
You can directly change its color and texture.  

In the previous version,  
when you set the color of the clothing and apply other materials,  
you could only switch to other applications via the control key.  
You could not modify the default behavior.  

From this version,  
you can modify the usual application in the user settings  
to make the process more efficient.  

Go to the main menu at the top,  
then click on User Customization,  
select Other Options,  
and then find Chess Color.  
Choose the application you want to use to apply new materials.  

Here, change it to the link option applied to all chess colors.  
Then click the Close button to save the settings.  

Now let’s check whether the new application has been set up.  
In the object window,  
go to the fabric options card,  
then click the Add button to create a new fabric.  
Next, drag this fabric to the pocket panel.  
You will see a tool hint behind the mouse cursor.  
It shows that the link option we just selected is activated.  

After clicking Update,  
you will see that the new fabric has been applied to all chess colors  
and there is a link.  

Please note that even after restarting the software,  
this application option will still be used.  

Through the optimized chess editor,  
you can easily and efficiently create and edit chess costumes.  
In the new version,  
you can arrange materials more freely.  
When you want to keep the original fabric,  
you can also change the pattern of the fabric.  
And when you finish other fabrics,  
there is a simpler way to achieve this.  

First, let’s switch to cherry blossom release mode.  
At this time, you can see that the large fabric of the dress has been finished.  

In general, for patterned fabrics,  
you may want to keep the current pattern result  
after making the pattern in the reference text.  

We can now separate the other fabrics to make the pattern.  
First, switch to the denim fabric to adjust the pattern settings.  
The design is transparent from front to back.  
Long press the original pattern function.  
You can see that there are currently two supported patterns:  
the front and back fabrics of the pattern.  

You can switch to the front fabric of the pattern.  
Just do the pattern on the front fabric.  
After the pattern is completed,  
let’s switch to the pattern fabric.  
You can see that the pattern fabric  
has retained the original pattern result.  

In addition to the above situation, this function can also help you achieve faster  
processing speed when you only need to assemble a certain fabric with multiple pieces of clothing.  

I hope this function can help you process more freely and flexibly.  

In the new version, the UV editing mode has become a UV editor.  
This can help you reduce operational steps and optimize workflow.  

In addition, a new UV expansion function has been added.  
It can display and prepare the texture of the back and sides of the fabric.  

Next, let’s see how to operate it together.  

In the UV editor window, find the UV coordinate position of the leather fabric.  
You can see that the front, back, and sides of the leather are different.  

Select all sheets of leather applied.  
Find UV expansion in the property editor.  
Below UV expansion, you can see the options for back and sides.  

When selecting back, the selected sheet will display the texture of the leather back.  
When selecting side, the selected sheet will display the texture of the leather side.  

If you find that after selecting UV expansion, the UV editor does not display the back and side textures,  
please check if the thick texture surface of the 3D window has been enabled.  
Then, select all sheets to automatically fill in the UV.  

Next, let’s see how to prepare the back and side textures of the leather.  

In the toolbar on the right side of the UV editor, click on the back and side texture of the leather.  

As before, you can set the storage path and UV area of the UV texture in the back and side texture window,  
and select the texture type you need.  

Click Save after setting it up.  
This is the saved UV texture.  

Please note that when downloading the customized clothing file in lower versions,  
the UV expansion default is off.  
This is to keep the existing UV layout.  
If you force it on, the previously hidden UV may appear by accident,  
thereby damaging the expected UV layout.  

If the applied fabric has the same back and side texture,  
and only the side is different, you can select only the side.  

This function can be applied to 3D files of wool, leather, and other fabrics.  

If this type of file needs to be exported as an FBX color file and edited in third-party software,  
then the handling of back and side textures will be very useful.  

Let’s look at FBX in more detail.  

You can create different elevated layers using a tool linked to the back and side texture.  

If the FBX load area is used,  
the UV texture of the back and side texture can be adjusted,  
and the coloring of the back and side texture can be changed.  

The Seoul International UMA 1080p ATA 2 night camera is working well.  
Press the button to see if you want to change the number or speed of the pedal.  

If the photo you want to play is running on the back and side texture,  
the back and side texture will be set to alternate.

chunks.title: CLO 2025.0 - Modes & Editor
chunks.content: ## CLO 2025.0 Modes & Editor Overview This document covers the key updates and features introduced in CLO version 2025.0, focusing on the chess editor, material color management, UV editing enhancements, and workflow optimizations for fabric and texture handling. Terminology includes "chess editor," "color blocks," "UV editor," "UV expansion," and "fabric texture surfaces." --- ## Chess Editor Updates and Color Block Management This section details enhancements to the chess editor interface, color block functionality, and component color editing, improving efficiency in applying and switching fabric colors and textures. - **Opening the Chess Editor:** The shortcut key **O** remains the same for quickly opening the chess editor window. - **Direct Color Block Switching:** Previously, hovering over a color block in the object window showed a prompt with the current chess color. In 2025.0, users can directly switch the color of a single color block without opening the chess editor. This applies not only to fabric but also to other materials such as buttons or costume names by clicking on their color blocks. - **Front, Side, and Back Fabric Views:** The chess editor now visually divides fabric textures by surface: front, side, and back. Each surface can be individually edited for color and texture using corresponding color blocks. - **Surface-Specific Color Blocks:** If the back or side fabric differs from the front, separate color blocks appear for those surfaces. For example, if only the reverse side differs, two color blocks will be shown: one for the front and one for the back. - **Uniform Surface Materials:** To use the same material and color for all fabric surfaces, simply select and click the fabric in the object window. The chess editor will display a single color block representing all surfaces. - **Independent Component Editing with Tree Structure:** Independent components (e.g., a pig’s nose button) are now displayed in a tree-shaped structure in the chess editor. Expanding the component name reveals individual color blocks for each part. Selecting a color block highlights the corresponding 3D model part for direct color and texture modification. --- ## Customizing Material Application Behavior Users can now customize how materials are applied to fabrics, improving workflow efficiency compared to earlier versions where the control key was required to switch applications. - **User Settings for Application Behavior:** Navigate to **Main Menu > User Customization > Other Options > Chess Color** to select the preferred application method for applying new materials. - **Link Option for All Chess Colors:** Setting the application to “Link” applies new fabrics across all chess colors simultaneously. - **Persistence Across Sessions:** This setting persists after restarting the software. - **Verification Example:** Creating a new fabric and dragging it to a pocket panel will show a tool hint confirming the link option is active. After clicking Update, the fabric applies to all chess colors with a link. --- ## Patterned Fabric and Cherry Blossom Release Mode This section explains how to maintain fabric patterns and improve processing speed when working with multiple fabric pieces.

chunks.content: - **Persistence Across Sessions:** This setting persists after restarting the software. - **Verification Example:** Creating a new fabric and dragging it to a pocket panel will show a tool hint confirming the link option is active. After clicking Update, the fabric applies to all chess colors with a link. --- ## Patterned Fabric and Cherry Blossom Release Mode This section explains how to maintain fabric patterns and improve processing speed when working with multiple fabric pieces. - **Cherry Blossom Release Mode:** Allows viewing of completed large fabric areas on a dress. - **Pattern Preservation:** When working with patterned fabrics, you can separate fabrics to preserve the current pattern after editing. - **Pattern Editing Workflow:** 1. Switch to the fabric you want to adjust (e.g., denim). 2. Use the long-press original pattern function supporting front and back fabric patterns. 3. Edit the front fabric pattern. 4. Switch to the pattern fabric to verify the original pattern result is retained. - **Use Case:** Useful for faster processing when assembling multiple clothing pieces with shared fabric. --- ## UV Editor Enhancements and UV Expansion Function The UV editing mode has been upgraded to a UV editor with added functionality for back and side fabric textures, streamlining texture management. - **UV Editor Features:** - Displays UV coordinates for the front, back, and sides of fabrics like leather. - UV expansion options allow toggling display and preparation of back and side textures. - **Using UV Expansion:** 1. Select all relevant fabric sheets in the UV editor. 2. In the property editor, enable UV expansion for back and/or side textures. 3. If back or side textures do not appear, ensure “thick texture surface” is enabled in the 3D window and reselect all sheets. - **Back and Side Texture Preparation:** - Accessible via toolbar icons in the UV editor. - Allows setting storage paths, UV layout, and texture type for back and side textures. - After setup, save the UV texture. - **Compatibility and Cautions:** - Lower versions of CLO have UV expansion off by default to preserve existing UV layouts. Forcing it on may reveal hidden UVs and disrupt layouts. - If back and side textures are identical except for a difference on the side, only the side can be selected for UV expansion. - **Supported Fabrics:** Applicable to 3D files of wool, leather, and similar materials. --- ## FBX Export and Third-Party Editing Support The UV expansion and back/side texture handling enhance interoperability with third-party software. - **FBX Color File Export:** Back and side textures can be exported and adjusted in FBX format for external editing. - **Elevated Layers:** Tools linked to back and side textures allow creation of different elevated layers, improving detail control. - **Coloring Adjustments:** Using the FBX load area, users can modify UV textures and recolor back and side textures after export.
